data_description.git_email: The email that will appear as the commit author.

remote_authentication_failed_token.title: Git remote rejected the credentials
remote_authentication_failed_token.description:
git-ha-ppens could not authenticate with the Git remote during `{operation}`. Configuration changes are still committed locally but are not synchronized.

Remote response: `{error}`

The personal access token has most likely expired, been revoked, or lacks the required permissions. Submit this repair to enter a new token.

remote_authentication_failed.title: Git remote rejected the credentials
remote_authentication_failed.description:
git-ha-ppens could not authenticate with the Git remote during `{operation}`. Configuration changes are still committed locally but are not synchronized.

Remote response: `{error}`

Check the credentials under **Settings → Devices & services → git-ha-ppens → Configure**. For SSH, make sure the key exists and is authorized for the repository. This repair disappears after the next successful synchronization.

push_rejected_email_privacy.title: GitHub rejected the push because of a private email address
push_rejected_email_privacy.description:
GitHub rejected the push during `{operation}` because at least one commit would publish a private email address. Configuration changes are still committed locally but are not synchronized.

Remote response: `{error}`

1. Copy your noreply address from the [GitHub email settings]({github_email_settings_url}).
2. Enter it as **Git email** under **Settings → Devices & services → git-ha-ppens → Configure → General Settings**. This only applies to new commits.
3. Commits that were already created locally still contain the old address. Back up your configuration, temporarily turn off **Enable auto-commit** in the same settings, then rewrite these commits in a terminal inside the repository directory: `git rebase origin/main --exec 'git commit --amend --no-edit --reset-author'`. Replace `main` with your branch; if nothing has been pushed yet, use `--root` instead of `origin/main`. If the rebase stops with a conflict, `git rebase --abort` restores the previous state. Turn **Enable auto-commit** back on afterwards. Alternatively, temporarily turn off **Block command line pushes that expose my email** in the GitHub email settings; the old address then becomes part of the published history.
4. Then press the **Push** button. This repair disappears after the next successful push.

push_rejected_protected_branch.title: The Git remote protects this branch
push_rejected_protected_branch.description:
The Git remote rejected the push during `{operation}` because the branch is protected. Configuration changes are still committed locally but are not synchronized.

Remote response: `{error}`

1. Open the branch protection rules or rulesets of the repository on your Git host.
2. Allow the account or token used by git-ha-ppens to push directly to this branch, or remove the protection. Rules that require pull requests, reviews, status checks, or signed commits block automatic pushes.
3. Then press the **Push** button. This repair disappears after the next successful push.

push_rejected_file_too_large.title: The Git remote rejected a file that is too large
push_rejected_file_too_large.description:
The Git remote rejected the push during `{operation}` because a commit contains a file above the size limit of the host. Configuration changes are still committed locally but are not synchronized.

Remote response: `{error}`

1. Find the file name in the remote response or the Home Assistant logs and exclude the file in `.gitignore` using the git-ha-ppens options.
2. Deleting the file in a new commit is not enough, because it remains part of the commits that were not pushed yet. Back up your configuration, then run `git reset --soft "$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)"` and `git rm --cached -- FILE` in a terminal inside the repository directory. Replace `main` with your branch and `FILE` with the path; if nothing has been pushed yet, use `git update-ref -d HEAD` instead of the first command. Your files stay unchanged; the next commit combines all changes that were not pushed yet.
3. Then press the **Push** button. This repair disappears after the next successful push.

push_rejected_non_fast_forward.title: Local and remote Git history have diverged
push_rejected_non_fast_forward.description:
The Git remote rejected the push during `{operation}` because the remote branch contains commits that are missing locally and could not be merged automatically. Remote commits are never overwritten. Configuration changes are still committed locally but are not synchronized.

Remote response: `{error}`

1. Press the **Pull** button. If it succeeds, no manual merge is needed.
2. If there is a merge conflict, run `git pull --no-rebase` in a terminal inside the repository directory, resolve the conflicts, and commit the result. Check the configuration before restarting Home Assistant.
3. Then press the **Push** button. This repair disappears after the next successful push.

push_rejected_other.title: The Git remote rejected the push
push_rejected_other.description:
The Git remote rejected the push during `{operation}`. Configuration changes are still committed locally but are not synchronized.

Remote response: `{error}`

1. Read the remote response above and the Home Assistant logs. Common causes are repository rules, detected secrets, missing token permissions (for example for workflow files), an exceeded storage quota, or a server-side hook.
2. Fix the cause on your Git host or in the affected commits. If the host had a temporary problem, the next automatic push may already succeed.
3. Then press the **Push** button. This repair disappears after the next successful push.

stale_index_lock.title: Automatic commits are blocked by a Git index lock
stale_index_lock.description:
git-ha-ppens could not safely remove the stale Git index lock at `{lock_path}`. Automatic commits remain blocked, so local configuration changes may not be committed or pushed.

1. Make sure no Git operation is currently running for this repository.
2. Remove `{lock_path}` using a terminal or file editor.
3. Wait for the next auto-commit interval or make another configuration change.

This repair will disappear automatically after git-ha-ppens confirms that the lock is gone.

unsafe_repository_layout.title: Git operations are blocked by an embedded repository

init.title: Resolve the embedded Git repository
init.description:
git-ha-ppens intentionally stopped Git mutations because files below `{paths}` might be missing from the outer backup. Assessment: `{reason}`.

Automatic migration is offered only for a single, clearly identified ESPHome Device Builder repository. All other layouts must be repaired manually.

migrate_esphome.title: Migrate ESPHome into the main repository
migrate_esphome.description:
This moves `/config/esphome/.git` into a private recovery directory below the outer Git metadata and stages the actual ESPHome files in the outer index. Existing inner history is retained in the recovery copy and is not merged. The operation will stop if the repositories or index no longer match the verified safe state.

Before continuing, make sure ESPHome cannot write version-history data:

1. Open the ESPHome Device Builder Web UI. On Home Assistant OS or Supervised, go to **Settings → Apps → ESPHome Device Builder** and select **Open Web UI**.
2. Open the menu in the top-right corner and select **Settings**.
3. Under **Appearance**, enable **Expert Mode**, then turn off **Save version history**.

Alternatively, stop the ESPHome add-on or Device Builder. Current assessment: `{reason}`.

data.confirm_esphome_stopped: I confirm that ESPHome is stopped or Save version history is disabled

data_description.confirm_esphome_stopped: This prevents ESPHome from recreating its repository while the atomic migration is running.

manual.title: Repair the embedded repository manually
manual.description:
Affected paths: `{paths}`.

1. Make sure the app that owns the embedded repository cannot write to it. For ESPHome, open the Device Builder Web UI, then use the top-right menu to open **Settings**. Under **Appearance**, enable **Expert Mode** and turn off **Save version history**. Alternatively, stop ESPHome.
2. Using the official Terminal & SSH app, preserve the inner repository outside `/config`: `esphome_backup="/backup/esphome-git-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"; mkdir -p "$esphome_backup"; mv /config/esphome/.git "$esphome_backup/dot-git"`. Never delete it before checking the remote backup.
3. If `git -C /config ls-files --stage -- esphome` shows mode `160000`, run `git -C /config rm --cached -f -- esphome`.
4. Make sure secrets and runtime data are ignored, then run `git -C /config add -A -- esphome`.
5. Confirm that YAML files use mode `100644`, while no `160000`, `secrets.yaml`, `.esphome/`, key, or pairing files are staged. Commit or sync the ESPHome path.
6. Submit this form to recheck the layout. Keep the backup until the remote contains the expected files.

error.confirm_required: Confirm that ESPHome cannot write version-history data before migrating.
error.migration_failed: The repository changed or did not meet every safety requirement. Nothing was intentionally published; review the logs and use the manual repair path.
error.recheck_failed: The repository layout could not be checked. Review the Home Assistant logs and try again.
error.still_unsafe: An embedded repository or Gitlink is still present. Complete the manual steps, then recheck.

abort.entry_removed: The related git-ha-ppens configuration entry no longer exists.

create_entry.migration_successful: ESPHome is now staged as regular files in the outer repository. The original inner Git metadata and an outer-index snapshot remain at `{backup_path}`. Auto-Commit will commit the snapshot when enabled; otherwise use Commit or Sync. Verify the remote backup before removing the recovery directory manually, then restart ESPHome if it was stopped. You may turn Save version history back on if you want per-save ESPHome commits; ESPHome should then report `/config` as its Git work tree.
create_entry.manual_fix_complete: The repository layout is safe again. git-ha-ppens has scheduled a reload. Verify that the expected ESPHome files reach the remote before removing your manual backup.

large_git_garbage.title: Git repository contains large leftover data
large_git_garbage.description:
The Git directory of this repository contains {garbage_size} GiB of leftover temporary files from interrupted Git operations. They are not part of your configuration history and only use disk space.

Run the `git_ha_ppens.gc` action, or enable **Automatic Git garbage collection** under **Settings → Devices & services → git-ha-ppens → Configure**. Git only removes leftovers older than two weeks, because newer files may still belong to a running Git operation. This repair disappears once less than 1 GiB of leftover data remains.

discard_changes.name: Discard Local Changes
discard_changes.description: Permanently discard staged and unstaged changes to tracked files. Untracked files are preserved.

gc.name: Garbage Collection
gc.description: Remove leftover temporary Git files older than two weeks and optimize the repository. History is never rewritten.
